 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE KULDEEP MATHUR Order 16/02/2024 This application for bail under Section 439 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the petitioner who has been arrested in connection with FIR No.466/2022 registered at Police Station Ratangarh, District Churu, for offences under Sections 450 and 376(2)(n) IPC.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner, who is aged about 42 years, has been roped in a false criminal case by the prosecutrix who is aged about 45 years and is a mature married woman.
Learned counsel submitted that the prosecutrix in the FIR stated that about 3 months prior to the date of lodging of the FIR, she was subjected to sexual assault by the present petitioner.

Learned counsel submitted that in the FIR, it has further been stated that the petitioner had snapped obscene photographs of the prosecutrix and threatened her to circulate the [2024:RJ-JD:8282] (2 of 4) [CRLMB-1578/2024] same on the social media platforms and thereby blackmailing her, subjected her to repeated sexual assault at different places.
Drawing attention of the Court towards challan papers, learned counsel submitted that as a matter of fact, the petitioner and prosecutrix were having consensual sexual relationship.

However, on their Surendra Kumar vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:8282) on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144892252/
1 relations turning strained, the petitioner has been falsely implicated in the present case.

sentences.text: Learned counsel submitted that the prosecutrix while being in the company of the petitioner, not only travelled with him to various places but also stayed with him in hotels situated in thickly populated area.
The prosecutrix thus despite having ample opportunities of disclosing the factum of she being blackmailed or subjected to forcible sexual assault by the petitioner did not tell anyone about the same.

Learned counsel further submitted that no obscene photographs allegedly used by the petitioner to blackmail and committing repeated sexual assault upon the prosecutrix have been recovered by the investigating agency.
It was urged that the charge-sheet has not even been filed against the petitioner for the offences under the Information Technology Act.

Lastly, learned counsel submitted that the petitioner is in judicial custody, challan has been filed and the trial of the case will take sufficiently long time, therefore, the benefit of bail should be granted to the accused-petitioner.
Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor and learned counsel for the complainant have vehemently opposed the bail application.

Learned counsel submitted that there is specific allegation against the petitioner of committing sexual assault upon the prosecutrix [2024:RJ-JD:8282] (3 of 4)
[CRLMB-1578/2024] by threatening to circulate her obscene photographs on the social medical platforms and, therefore, looking to the seriousness of the accusation levelled against the petitioner,
he does not deserve to be enlarged on bail.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Public Prosecutor and learned counsel for the complainant.
Perused the material available on record.

Having considered the rival submissions, facts and circumstances of the case, this Court prima facie finds that the FIR has been lodged against the petitioner after a delay of 3 months from the date on which the prosecutrix was allegedly first time subjected to sexual assault by the petitioner.

This Court also prima facie finds that sufficient material is available on record indicating that the prosecutrix not only travelled with the petitioner to various places but also stayed with him in hotels.
It can thus be presumed that she had ample opportunities of disclosing the factum of she being subjected to forcible sexual assault or blackmail by the petitioner.

This Court also prima facie finds that specific allegation has been levelled against the present petitioner that he threatened/blackmailed the prosecutrix to circulate her obscene photographs and subjected her to repeated forcible sexual assault.
However, no such obscene photographs have been recovered by the investigating agency.
The charge- sheet has not even been filed against the petitioner for the offence under Information Technology Act.
Thus, without expressing any opinion on merits/demerits of the case, this Court is inclined to enlarge the petitioner on bail.

[2024:RJ-JD:8282] (4 of 4) [CRLMB-1578/2024] Accordingly, the bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. is allowed and it is ordered that the accused-petitioner- Surendra Kumar S/o Sunda Ram @ Om Prakash shall be enlarged on bail in connection with FIR No.466/2022 registered at Police Station Ratangarh, District Churu, provided he furnishes a personal bond in the sum of Surendra Kumar vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:8282) on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144892252/
2 Rs.50,000/- with two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the learned trial Judge for his appearance before the court concerned on all the dates of hearing as and when called upon to so.
